chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: “May Allah keep you well. News of your illness has reached us and we have become apprehensive, so if only you would inform us or teach us.” He said: “Ali عليه السلام was knowledgeable, and knowledge is inherited. Thus no knowledgeable one perishes except that there remains after him one who knows the like of his knowledge, or whatever Allah wills.”

I said: “Is there then any leeway for the people, when the knowledgeable one dies, not to recognize the one after him?” He said: “As for the people of this city, no”—meaning al-Madinah—“but as for other towns, then according to the extent of their travel.” Indeed, Allah says:

“And it is not for the believers to go forth all together. So why should not a group from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them, so that they may beware?”

He said: I said, “What do you say about one who dies during that?” He said: “He is in the position of one who leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then death overtakes him; his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah.”
He said: I said, “Then when they arrive, by what thing do they recognize their master?” He said: “He is granted tranquillity, dignity, and awe.”

key_terms.السَّكِينَةَ: divinely bestowed tranquillity marking the rightful Imam
key_terms.الْعَالِمُ: the one endowed with authoritative divine knowledge
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: the divinely inherited knowledge possessed by the Imam
key_terms.لِيَتَفَقَّهُوا: to gain deep understanding in religion
key_terms.يُتَوَارَثُ: is passed down in succession from one rightful bearer to another

ai.seo_question: How are people obligated to recognize the Imam after the death of the previous Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that divine knowledge among the Imams عليهم السلام is inherited and does not cease with the death of one Imam. It explains the duty of people to recognize the Imam after the passing of the previous one, while accounting for practical limits of distance and travel. It also describes signs by which the rightful Imam is recognized, namely tranquillity, dignity, and awe.
